item.title: 2027: DSS uncovers plot against NYSC members, arrests suspects – INEC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has disclosed that the people behind a plot against the Commission’s Ad Hoc staff, especially Youth Corps members, have been uncovered and arrested and would be prosecuted soon. Prof. Amupitan made the disclosure in Enugu at the South-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. According to the Commission’s Daily Bulletin, INEC recently identified potential risks to its Ad Hoc staff, “especially Youth Corps members,” and has taken measures to neutralise the threat. He said the people behind the plot were uncovered by the Department of State Services DSS. The INEC Chairman added that the Commission plans to host a Security Conference “very soon” to address other issues relating to election security. On the Commission’s wider security arrangements, he said its partnership with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been reinvigorated and expanded. Prof. Amupitan said INEC was working with security agencies at national and state levels, using its Election Risk Management ERM tools, to develop “a robust, intelligence-driven security architecture.” He also identified a lingering public trust deficit, voter apathy and the rising tide of misinformation and disinformation as the Commission’s greatest challenges. “A single malicious fake news post, an unverified rumour, or a deepfake video can travel across millions of screens in seconds,” he warned. He said false narratives only gain traction when the Commission’s administrative execution falters. “The conduct, competence, and character of our staff in the field are either our strongest defence against fake news, or its biggest catalyst,” he stated. The INEC Chairman said the Commission’s response would be “proactive transparency, swift official communication, and uncompromising operational precision at every polling unit.” On discipline, Prof. Amupitan said, “Partisan leaning, administrative negligence, extortion, or compromised ethics will not be tolerated under my leadership.” He reminded staff that Section 26 of the Electoral Act 2026 requires all staff, Electoral Officers, Presiding Officers, Returning Officers and participating security officials to swear an oath of loyalty and neutrality. “The question governing your actions must never be ‘Who will benefit from this decision?’ The question must always be ‘What does the law require me to do?'” he said. item.title: CVR: INEC reviews registration records, PVC bottlenecks in S’East

The Commission in its Daily Bulletin said Amupitan gave the directive on Tuesday in Enugu at the South-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. item.title: Ebola: Avoid unnecessary physical contact, Academy of Medical Sciences cautions
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe The Academy of Medical Sciences of Nigeria has urged Nigerians to be wary of handshakes, hugs and other unnecessary physical contact and to adopt non-contact greetings instead as part of the immediate nationwide high alert response to the confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. In a public health advisory issued on Tuesday, the Academy endorsed the Federal Government’s response to the confirmed case involving a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria from Uganda, the Academy commended the prompt isolation of the patient, commencement of contact tracing and intensified surveillance. Noting that the measure was an additional precaution members of the public were urged to wash their hands regularly with soap and water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons and refrain from handling the bodies of people suspected to have died from Ebola. The advisory, jointly signed by the Academy’s President, Emeritus Professor Osato Giwa-Osagie; Foundation President, Professor Oladapo A. Ashiru; and Rapid Response Committee member, Professor Boaz Adegboro, urged the federal government to extend heightened preparedness measures across the country, drawing on Nigeria’s successful containment of Ebola in 2014 and its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. In the statement, the experts called for enhanced screening at airports, seaports and land borders, particularly for travellers arriving from countries affected by Ebola, as well as the activation of isolation and treatment centres across states. Nigeria’s Ebola Outbreak Explained Nigeria’s experience with Ebola Nigeria’s experience with Ebola in 2014 demonstrated how quickly an imported infection could become a national public health emergency in a country with a large population and busy international travel routes. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. His arrival triggered an emergency response involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Lagos State Government, the NCDC and international health partners. According to a report published in the United States Centres for Disease Control and Prevention’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases, comprising 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, by September 24, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014. The country identified and monitored 894 contacts during the response, while 11 patients with laboratory-confirmed Ebola were discharged from care. How prepared is the country for Ebola? Nigeria’s latest preparedness efforts began before the reported FCT case. On June 9, 2026, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu approved the immediate release of N10 billion as emergency intervention funding for public health preparedness and response. The fund is separate from a N21.2 million per-state disbursement under the State Outbreak Investigation and Response Fund. The Presidency also announced the establishment of a Presidential Task Force on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats, chaired by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. According to the State House, the fund was intended to strengthen the operational capacity of the NCDC and support critical national public health emergency response activities. The government also directed states hosting international airports and international border corridors, alongside relevant ministries, departments and agencies, to submit their preparedness plans, funding requirements and intervention needs. The measures announced included intensified passenger screening at international airports, enhanced monitoring of passengers arriving through designated high-risk routes, and the activation of referral and isolation centres at the Lagos and Abuja international airports. Other proposed measures included health declaration systems for passengers arriving from or transiting through designated high-risk countries and improved coordination among health, immigration, aviation and security authorities. In a May 28, 2026, advisory, the NCDC assessed Nigeria’s risk of importation as high, citing regional transmission, international travel, population movement, porous land borders and the difficulty of distinguishing early Ebola symptoms from common illnesses such as malaria and Lassa fever. item.title: London/Paris Club refunds: Court voids EFCC probe report
item.description: …Faults FG over probe of ALGON lawyer By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA—A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, sitting in Garki, yesterday, set aside an investigation report by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, which alleged fraud in the London/Paris Club refunds involving the 774 local government areas in the country. In the judgment, Justice Suleiman Belgore faulted the Federal Government for directing the anti-graft agency to investigate the matter despite two separate court decisions. The judge held that the Federal Government acted beyond its powers by directing the EFCC, through the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, to investigate court judgments ordering payment to a consultant, Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, for legal services rendered in the matter. Justice Belgore noted that the directive came after the government had issued promissory notes for the payment following a clearance report by the Department of State Services, DSS. He held that the EFCC’s subsequent report amounted to an affront to the authority of the court. “The law and the court must be respected. They are both official and statutory. It is not within the powers of the Respondents to use Exhibit GG to impugn the integrity of the court by claiming the judgement was obtained fraudulently,” he held. The judge said the appropriate course for the Federal Government was to file processes seeking to set aside the judgments rather than investigate them. “There were negotiated terms of engagement between the Incorporated Trustees of ALGON and the applicant. These terms of engagement were renegotiated by parties in open court on September 15, 2016,” Justice Belgore added. He held that the 10 promissory notes issued to Iseghohi-Edwards in compliance with a valid order of mandamus made against the Federal Government by the Federal High Court were validly issued by former President Muhammadu Buhari. Consequently, the court upheld the suit filed by the Abuja-based lawyer, holding that there was unassailable evidence that he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, ALGON, to represent the 774 local government areas in the London/Paris Club refunds matter. Among the reliefs granted, the court barred the Federal Government and its agencies from arresting, detaining or prosecuting the plaintiff, or infringing on his fundamental rights in connection with the matter. item.title: Uduaghan’s remains arrive Delta as tributes pour in
item.description: •Oborevwori, Obi, Obaseki, others pay tribute By Dapo Akinrefon, Jimitota Onoyume & Ochuko Akuopha WARRI—The remains of former Delta State governor, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan, arrived in the state, yesterday, as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and his wife, Tobore Oborevwori, joined members of the late governor’s family to receive them at Osubi Airport, Okpe Local Government Area of the state. Oborevwori and his wife later visited the family at the deceased’s residence in Warri, where they commiserated with his widow, Deaconess Roli Uduaghan. The governor described the late Uduaghan as his boss, recalling the political support he received from him and his appointment as one of his special advisers in 2007. “He contributed immensely to the development of Delta State, most especially the Asaba International Airport. item.title: Currency in circulation rises 81% to N5.4trn
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Currency in circulation in Nigeria rose by 81 per cent to N5.44 trillion in August 2026, from N3.01 trillion in August 2023, underscoring the continued strong demand for physical cash despite the rapid expansion of electronic payments over the past three years. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria’s, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics show that the strongest increase occurred between August 2023 and August 2024 when currency in circulation rose from N3.010 trillion in August 2023 to N4.55 trillion in August 2024, representing an increase of N1.54 trillion or 51.1 per cent. The growth moderated considerably in the following years. In August 2025, currency in circulation increased to N5.057 trillion, up N508 billion or 11.2 per cent from the previous year. By August 2026, the growth rate moderated further though it hit new threshold of N5.436 trillion, an increase of N379 billion or 7.5 per cent Year-on-Year, YoY. The figures therefore indicate that while the amount of physical cash in circulation has continued to rise, the pace of growth has slowed significantly, from 51.1 per cent in 2024 to 11.2 per cent in 2025 and 7.5 per cent in 2026. Banks’ reserves The increase in currency in circulation occurred alongside a substantial rise in banks’ reserves. According to the data supplied, banks’ reserves rose from N18.528 trillion in August 2023 to N25.456 trillion in August 2024, an increase of N6.928 trillion or 37.4 per cent. They increased further to N31.583 trillion in August 2025, before reaching N36.067 trillion in August 2026. Overall, banks’ reserves increased by N17.539 trillion, or 94.7 per cent, between August 2023 and August 2026. The CBN’s monetary statistics identify currency in circulation and banks’ reserves as components of reserve money or base money. Commenting on the development, David Adonri, Managing Director, High Cap Securities Limited, said: “When more money is held as physical cash, a portion of liquidity is outside the immediate deposit base of commercial banks and is therefore less available for banks to intermediate through loans and other financial assets. However, the rising currency stock should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of excessive liquidity or inflationary pressure. Demand for cash can also increase because of higher nominal prices, larger transaction values and the expansion of economic activity. The increase is particularly noteworthy because Nigeria has experienced rapid growth in electronic payments, mobile banking, fintech services and instant-payment platforms. The continued expansion of physical currency therefore suggests that Nigeria’s digital-payment revolution has not eliminated the country’s cash economy.” Vanguard News The post Currency in circulation rises 81% to N5.4trn appeared first on Vanguard News .

The World Bank says GDP grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026, against 3.9 per cent a year earlier, and projects average growth of 4.4 per cent through 2028. Inflation, which fell during 2025, has faced renewed pressure from higher fuel and transport costs. External reserves and public revenues have strengthened. World Trade Organisation (WTO) Director-General, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, credited Tinubu’s administration in 2025 for stabilising the economy. She stressed that the next tasks were growth, job creation and social safety nets. But stability is a foundation for prosperity, not prosperity itself. Tinubu’s government has taken difficult measures: implementing petrol subsidy removal, partially removing electricity subsidies, liberalising the naira and pursuing tax reforms. They have eased fiscal pressures, improved foreign exchange conditions and increased revenue available to governments. The World Bank says growth has stabilised for the first time since 2019. There is something profoundly civilising in this arrangement which Nigerian restructuring agitators seem to always overlook or remain unaware of. Instead of confronting one another through political pressure or public mobilisation, governments may appear as litigants and submit their claims to reasoned adjudication. Sovereignty under constitutional government is demonstrated not only through state power, but also through institutional dialogue, established procedures and acceptance of final lawful authority. The Supreme Court is an arbiter and national integrating institution. Its work helps to keep the disagreements of a diverse federation within a common constitutional language and culture. However, there is a paradox at the heart of judicial authority. Courts possess neither armies nor political constituencies. Judges do not campaign for votes, command the treasury or administer ministries, and remain largely invisible to the public. The strength of the judiciary rests upon something less tangible but enduring, which is public confidence in its independence, integrity and fidelity to law. This is why, in my humble opinion, judicial character matters. At the highest level, legal knowledge is indispensable but insufficient. A Supreme Court Justice must possess intellectual depth, patience, courage, independence of mind and awareness of institutional consequences. A judgment may settle one dispute while also establishing principles upon which many future controversies will be decided. A phrase written today can become part of the constitutional vocabulary of tomorrow. Judicial temperament therefore becomes an element of constitutional security. The qualities I observed in His Royal Highness, the Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad I — composure, measured deliberation, dignity and the ability to listen before concluding — are attributes essential to an institution expected to pronounce finally upon matters already surrounded by passion. Reasoned criticism forms part of constitutional democracy and can strengthen judicial authority. For this reason, Type Approval is not merely a regulatory requirement. Edoyemi Ogoh, who is Director, Technical Standards and Network Integrity at NCC. “The initiative,” he continued, “supports the Commission’s broader efforts to strengthen the integrity of devices in Nigeria’s telecommunications sector. It will improve compliance with applicable standards, enhance network performance, facilitate the identification of non-compliant devices, and strengthen consumer confidence in devices sold and used within the country.” The NCC Device Checker has been long in the making, like the meat of the antelope, which takes long to cook in order to achieve maximum delicacy. The regulator said it has consulted with stakeholders across the value chain, which include the Nigeria Customs Service, Original Equipment Manufacturers, importers and relevant market associations, adding that “this collaborative approach reflects our belief that effective regulation is best achieved through partnership, consultation and shared responsibility, consistent with firm belief in collaboration.” In my very simple observation, the regulator is waging a full-fledged war against the grey market through which millions of devices pour into the Nigerian market, phone theft, which is prevalent in this part of the world – a stolen phone can now easily be knocked off the networks – and ensuring the fidelity of products. Phone buyers are investing in genuine products that can deliver proper service by following the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number at the back of the phone pack or even doing the needful to confirm second-hand phones. As one industry source told this writer, this would also mean the Customs Service making more money through revenue generation, because, at the moment, it was possible for cars or buses to be imported into Nigeria with lots of phones in them which are not properly cleared or even have their sources determined, except that their destination is Nigeria. The Device Checker has drawn a line against such practices. Understandably, not everybody is excited about the NCC Device Checker. The Association of Mobile Phones and Allied Products Traders of Nigeria has raised some concerns about the introduction of the Device Checker, asking the NCC to provide a window of sensitisation in order to align all stakeholders with its plans. Even as they support the fight against counterfeit devices, the association is frowning at sundry fees that may be introduced, which could bring more hardship on its members and phone and device buyers. But what is this thing about counterfeit devices? I will tell a personal story. I have an iPad which plays a central role in all my operations. Recently, the charger got bad, and I decided to buy one from a shopping mall nearby before heading out to Banex Plaza to buy an original version the following day. I plugged the iPad with the stop-gap charger and stepped out of the room for some minutes. By the time I returned, the room was charged and very hot. My mind went to the iPad, which was as hot as fire itself. Just a few minutes’ delay, and it would have exploded into a ball of fire. I was lucky because the damage was not extensive. But it still cost about N400,000 to bring it back to life! The nation’s telecommunications sector is growing in leaps and bounds; it therefore demands the attention of the regulator to ensure that such growth is not impaired by fake equipment or allow such equipment to endanger the lives of users. The regulator is waging a war against what the people may ignorantly accept as good and normal, and, in the process, save their lives. Even with all the good attributes of the Device Checker, which could include restoring efficiency to the mobile networks, hyperbolically, and causing subscribers to smile each time a connection is made – oh, thinking of nirvana – I was also very fascinated with what the Device Checker is not, according to the NCC. This is very important in a country where the trust deficit is nearly as important as the country’s legal tender and the politicians are skilled in making falsehood the figment of reality. “The Commission recognizes that consumers have legitimate expectations regarding the privacy and security of their personal information. The Type Approval Compliance framework is not designed for surveillance and does not provide the Commission with access to the content of communications, photographs, messages, contacts, financial information or any other personal information stored on users’ devices. The framework is limited to device identification information required to support regulatory compliance and facilitate the identification of devices that may not meet applicable Type Approval requirements. It further proposed that the governorship should move to Ebonyi Central in 2031 and remain there for eight years before moving to Ebonyi South in 2039 for another eight years. The proposed rotation schedule provides for Ebonyi North from 2023 to 2031, Ebonyi Central from 2031 to 2039 and Ebonyi South from 2039 to 2047. The stakeholders also called for the equitable distribution of public amenities and development projects among the zones, stressing the need to sustain fairness, justice and peaceful coexistence. On governance, the summit commended Nwifuru’s administration for its development initiatives under the People’s Charter of Needs. It identified infrastructure and rural development, education, healthcare, agriculture, food security, human capital development, women’s empowerment and youth development as important areas requiring sustained attention. The summit urged political leaders and other stakeholders to continue promoting dialogue across party lines and discourage actions capable of creating unnecessary tension during the transition period. It also called on political parties, aspirants, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to work towards peaceful, credible and orderly elections in 2027. item.description: Phil Foden hit a hat-trick to underline his long-awaited return to form as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday. After a significant dip over the last two seasons, Foden provided hope of a renaissance for the England playmaker with a sublime display at the Etihad Stadium. The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s win against Ipswich. Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace. Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival. Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest. Foden doubled City’s lead before the break and although Stavros Pilios pulled one back for the Greek side after the interval, the Premier League leaders finished with a flourish. Rayan Cherki bagged City’s third goal in typically flamboyant fashion and Foden struck twice more to complete his treble. It was City’s second win in the league phase after beating Porto in their opening game and losing to holders Paris Saint-Germain last week. City’s future remains in limbo as they wait the result of their appeal against an independent commission’s verdict that they were guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. item.title: PSG Overpower Barcelona For Third Champions League Win In A Row
item.description: Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League. The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes. item.title: ‘An Icon’: Tinubu, Makinde, Abiodun Pay Tribute To Afenifere Leader Fasoranti
